A_target.statement:
Let $V$ be a [[Definition:Finite Dimensional Vector Space|finite-dimensional]] [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] over $K$.
Then the evaluation map $\operatorname {ev}: V \to V^{**}$, $\map {\map {\operatorname {ev} } v} \phi = \map \phi v$, is a [[Definition:Natural Isomorphism|natural]] [[Definition:Linear Isomorphism|isomorphism]].

B_source.statement:
Let $V$ have basis $e_1, \ldots, e_n$.
Then the [[Definition:Dual Basis|dual functionals]] $e_i^*$ with $\map {e_i^*} {e_j} = \delta_{i j}$ form a basis of $V^*$, so $\dim V^* = \dim V$.

substitutions.the dual basis: a functional separating a given vector from 0

object_map.reformulation: Apply the dual-space construction twice; evaluation pairs V with V* in the reverse direction and needs no choice of basis.

validity_conditions: Finite dimension is essential: for infinite dimension, evaluation is injective but not surjective.
Naturality holds because ev is defined without choosing a basis.
proof_plan: $\map {\operatorname {ev} } v$ is linear in $\phi$, and $\operatorname {ev}$ is linear in $v$.

If $v \ne 0$, extend $v$ to a basis $e_1 = v, e_2, \ldots, e_n$.
Then $\map {e_1^*} v = 1$, so $\map {\operatorname {ev} } v \ne 0$, and $\operatorname {ev}$ is [[Definition:Injection|injective]].

Applying the source result twice, $\dim V^{**} = \dim V^* = \dim V$.
An injective linear map between spaces of equal finite dimension is an isomorphism.

For linear $T: V \to W$, $T^{**} \circ \operatorname {ev}_V = \operatorname {ev}_W \circ T$, so the isomorphism is natural.
{{qed}}
